title: fix: reroute MiniMax M2.7 to OpenRouter
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes the MiniMax M2.7 outage: the Fireworks route returned model-not-deployed 404s and produced 0/121 successful requests in the reported hour. Other Fireworks models remained healthy, so this is isolated to that deployment.
- Routes the existing canonical model and aliases to exact OpenRouter model minimax/minimax-m2.7, pinned to DeepInfra FP8 with provider fallback disabled. This prevents route and price drift. Azure is not used because it has no exact serverless M2.7 deployment.
- Makes the model paid-only and records the pinned endpoint rates: $0.25/M input, $0.05/M cached input, and $1.00/M output at multiplier 1. Public identity, aliases, reasoning, tools, and the no-Pollinations-fallback contract remain unchanged.
- Verified directly against OpenRouter: HTTP 200 from DeepInfra for text, reasoning, usage, and tool calling; reported cost reconciled exactly to the registry rates. Focused gen tests passed 83/83, Enter pricing and alias tests passed 512/512, the pricing snapshot was updated, both services typecheck, and Biome is clean.

gist.headline: MiniMax Finds a New Nest
gist.blurb: MiniMax M2.7 has moved to a working branch of the hive. Its aliases, reasoning, and tool calls are back in business, with the route pinned neatly in place.
gist.summary: Rerouted MiniMax M2.7 and its aliases from the unavailable Fireworks deployment to OpenRouter's exact DeepInfra FP8 endpoint, with paid-only pricing pinned at $0.25/M input, $0.05/M cached input, and $1.00/M output.
gist.impact: MiniMax M2.7 requests now return successfully for text, reasoning, usage reporting, and tool calling while preserving the existing model identity, aliases, and no-Pollinations-fallback behavior.
gist.visual_concept: Depict MiniMax M2.7 as a cozy glowing model seed being carefully rerouted from a quiet, crossed-out terminal path into a healthy OpenRouter garden pipeline labeled DeepInfra FP8. Polli, wearing a tiny network technician cap, guides the seed along the new cable-vine while a cheerful CRT monitor robot confirms a successful response; include small code-plants and a subtle pricing tag to represent the pinned endpoint and rates.
